content.value: How does the Ising Model determine magnetization in materials using the Metropolis Monte Carlo method?

<sub>(b)</sub> Suppose you have to select a copper alloy for the windings of an electromagnet designed to create very high magnetic field. The windings must sustain stresses much higher than pure copper can handle but alloying copper to increase its strength usually also decrease its conductivity which leads to undesirable increased heating of the windings. To get an increase in strength with minimum decrease in conductivity, should you use soluble or insoluble alloying elements? Justify your answer with proper examples.
